stops.name: Biosphärenreservat Thüringer Wald
stops.detail: The Biosphere Reserve Thuringian Forest is a UNESCO biosphere reserve in Thuringia between the cities of Suhl, Ilmenau and Schleusingen. It covers an area of 337 km2, consisting mainly of forests, mountain meadows, but also of high moorlands. The area is completely surrounded by the Thuringian Forest Nature Park. As early as 1939, the first areas of today's Biosphere Reserve were declared a nature reserve. It was declared in 1979 under the name Biosphere Reserve Vessertal with an area of 1384 ha as the first Biosphere Reserve in Germany. From [dated source] to [dated source], the area was called the Biosphere Reserve Vessertal-Thuringian Forest. In [dated source], it was renamed “Biosphere Reserve Thuringian Forest” and expanded to its current size.
